doctrines.question: Who is baptism for, and what does it effect?
doctrines.framing: Two questions travel together here: who may rightly be baptised, and what the water does. A view of the second usually settles the first.
doctrines.tier_note: Churches in full fellowship with one another differ on this, which places it below the doctrines that define the gospel itself.

open.todo: Work out whether the household baptisms in Acts and the covenant argument from circumcision in Colossians 2 carry the weight the paedobaptist case puts on them, and decide what baptism actually effects before deciding who receives it.

positions.label: Believers only
positions.hold: Baptism is for those who have professed faith, and it signifies the union with Christ they have already entered.
positions.why: Every baptism the New Testament narrates follows a profession of faith.
positions.vs: Infant baptism as the ordinary entry into the covenant community.

positions.label: Infant, covenantal
positions.hold: The children of believers are baptised as members of the covenant community, on the same ground as circumcision under the old covenant.
positions.why: The covenant sign was given to households, and the New Testament nowhere withdraws it from them.
positions.vs: Believers-only baptism as the exclusive New Testament pattern.

doctrines.question: In what sense is Christ present in the Lord's Supper?
doctrines.framing: The disagreement is not over whether the Supper matters but over what happens in it, and the answers range from a change in the elements themselves to a memorial that works on the memory.
doctrines.tier_note: Churches that recognise one another's baptisms have differed on this for five centuries.

open.todo: Work out what 'this is my body' claimed in its own setting, and decide whether the Supper conveys anything or only recalls something.

positions.label: Spiritual presence
positions.hold: Christ is truly present to faith in the Supper by the Spirit, without any change in the elements themselves.
positions.why: The Supper is a means of grace rather than a bare sign, and the Spirit unites the believer to the ascended Christ.
positions.vs: A purely memorial Supper in which nothing is received.

positions.label: Memorial
positions.hold: The Supper is a remembrance of Christ's death, in which the elements signify but do not convey his body and blood.
positions.why: Christ's command was to do this in remembrance of him, and the signs point to a finished work rather than repeat it.

held_by.citation: Baptist Faith and Message (2000), Article VII
